newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to cut corporate tax in budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to cut corporate tax in budget - paper.

text.p: The Portuguese government's 1997 budget proposals will include a corporate tax cut of between one and two percentage points, Publico daily quoted an official source as saying.

It said the state agreed to the proposal from the Portuguese Industry Confederation (CIP) in return for the CIP's support for minimum income tax payments of between 100,000 and 200,000 escudos a year by self-employed professionals.
Government officials were not immediately available to confirm the report.
Portuguese corporate tax, which taxes profits, is presently 36 percent.
The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres is due to present its 1997 budget proposals to parliament on October 15. Analysts expect the budget to be passed.

The government has promised tight control of spending and measures to boost revenue collection, including a crackdown on widespread tax evasion, to meet targets for joining the single European currency in 1999.
